title: BF16 prefill attention, two shardings of one mathematics
formula: out = softmax(Q @ K^T / sqrt(128)) @ V per batch, computed as score^T = K @ Q^T; BF16 Q[B*MQ,128], K/V[B*N,128] and out[B*MQ,128], FP32 score, exponentials and online state, BF16 P before the PV matmul
study_for: Read the transposition first, because every other choice here follows from it. The scores are computed as `score^T = K @ Q^T`, so `softmax_t_vf` works on [key=128, query=64]: keys are rows, queries are lanes, and the per-query maximum is four independent partial-max chains down the 128 key rows with a tree-combine. There is no cross-lane reduction anywhere in this kernel. If your scores are untransposed, the reduction is the part that does not transfer and you need a real cross-lane reduce instead.

The `flat.py` section of kernel.py is the clearest statement of software pipelining across tile boundaries in this tree: fusing the (M-tile, K-tile) loops into ONE linear `step` loop lets the lag-2 pipeline carry across M-tile boundaries, so M-tile B's QK ramp overlaps M-tile A's PV drain and the per-M-tile ramp/drain bubbles -- 2 QK-only and 2 PV-only trips each -- disappear. It also states the price: `k_tiles >= 2`, and the per-M-tile state has to be double-buffered by M-tile parity so A's drain and B's ramp do not share it.
What does NOT get double-buffered is as informative: `rmax` stays single, because only stage 1 touches it and stage 1 is strictly serial in `step`.

The `flat` and `fd` bodies are the same mathematics over two different shardings -- M-tiles only versus the flat (m_tile, k_tile) stream-K grid -- with the FD merge of two FP32 partial states and its explicit ties-away BF16 cast at the end. main.py runs the same four shapes through both, so the pair is directly comparable, and the two entrypoints share one copy of the geometry and the softmax/accumulate/finalise VFs because the two source modules defined them identically.
do_not_copy_when: You have one K-tile per M-tile. The lag-2 fusion needs at least two, and the parity double-buffering needs adjacent M-tiles to differ in parity -- which is why every `flat` case here has N > 128.

More than two cores can own one query tile in the `fd` sharding. The merge reads exactly two workspace slots per split tile, so a `block_dim` that cuts one M tile three ways, or that puts two interior boundaries in the same tile, merges the wrong pair without complaining. Each case names a block_dim that satisfies the precondition; it is not a free knob.
Your head dimension is not 128. D=128 is wired into both bodies as TILE_M/TILE_N=128 and two 64-lane FP32 register chunks per output row, and is not a parameter despite being a kernel argument.
